newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN appeals for $39.9 million for Iraqi people.
newsitem.headline: UN appeals for $39.9 million for Iraqi people.

text.p: A delay in implementing the oil-for-food plan for Iraq led the United Nations on Friday to appeal for $39.9 million in emergency aid to help civilians suffering from malnutrition and disease.
"Throughout Iraq, the majority of the civilian population is believed to be living below the poverty line," said U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa.
The situation is particularly acute in the northern Kurdish areas, scene of recent fighting, with malnutrition rampant, according to a statement from the Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA).

The oil-for-food plan, on hold because of the crisis in northern Iraq, would have allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil in order to buy badly needed supplies for its people, who are suffering under U.N. trade sanctions.
The embargoes were imposed in August 1991 after Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait. The United Nations said family incomes were currently only a fraction of pre-1991 levels.
The appeal, according to the DHA, is designed to meet emergency needs over the next three months until the oil-for-food programme can be implemented.

"The cumulative effects of economic sanctions, hyper-inflation, unemployment and a 30 percent drop in crop production this year have led to a disquieting level of hardship now suffered by vulnerable groups in Iraq," it said.
The recent conflict in Kurdish areas when President Saddam Hussein's armies entered to help one Kurdish faction has aggravated the situation with refugees fleeing the area.

DHA said schools, hospitals, water and sanitation systems and government buildings had been looted. In the city of Arbil, drinking water is scarce and blood banks, vaccines and medicines that need refrigeration cannot be used.
"Malnutrition is rampant and fewer than 50 percent of children and women are receiving more than half their calorific needs," it said.
Earlier appeals for Iraqi humanitarian aid fell far short of their mark, DHA said.
